task.approach: Schools approach: this slice is the school table for every neighborhood, the enrollment movement this cycle, the district card, and the students and teachers on the ledger. The quality table is stable cycle to cycle — never write as if a score moved when it did not; enrollment is the number that moves. Warm, precise. Never invent a named student or teacher; a score trend is colour unless it is on this table. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

subjects.name: Lila Bennington
subjects.profile: Lila Bennington — Oakland Unified Elementary Teacher

sources.name: Lila Bennington
sources.quote: Oh, I actually teach in Fruitvale, not Rockridge. But I can tell you that teaching anywhere in Oakland means constantly balancing the needs of so many different kids with what resources we actually have. The community here—when they show up for us—it makes all the difference. Just last week, one of my student's grandparents volunteered to help with reading circles. That kind of thing keeps me going.

sources.name: Aaron Whitfield
sources.quote: Rockridge schools have always been a point of pride for the neighborhood. The quality index speaks for itself, and it’s clear that families here value education deeply. Enrollment’s been steady, which tells me people are committed to maintaining that standard.

sources.name: Rick Walker
sources.quote: I hear Rockridge schools are top-notch, but honestly, it feels like we're always playing catch-up here in Fruitvale. Those numbers don't tell the whole story - it's about the community behind them.
